title: Kerala Tour Package Guide: Routes, Cost & Best Time
subtitle: Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and Alleppey — how the route works, what it costs, and how to shape it around your dates.
excerpt: Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and Alleppey — what a Kerala tour package covers, what it costs, when to go, and how to shape the route around your own dates.

contentSections.heading: What a Kerala tour package actually covers
contentSections.content: A Kerala trip is usually a hill station, the backwaters and a coastal or heritage town, spread across four to eight days depending on how much you want to see. Most travellers combine Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and Alleppey into one loop, and the order can be reversed or trimmed to fit your flights. The parts that make up a package are the same everywhere; what changes is the hotel category, the vehicle and how much is inside the price.
bulletPoints: Accommodation across 3-star, 4-star or 5-star properties, chosen to your budget
Private transport for sightseeing and the drives between towns, sized to the group
Meals as per the plan — breakfast in most packages, the rest optional
Sightseeing at each stop, planned around the days you have
A houseboat night in Alleppey or Kumarakom, where the itinerary includes one
Route, hotels, vehicle and activities all adjustable
contentSections.highlightQuote: Popular route: Kochi – Munnar – Thekkady – Alleppey. Best for couples, families and groups; four to eight days.

contentSections.heading: The four places most itineraries are built from
contentSections.content: Almost every Kerala package is some arrangement of these four, and knowing what each one is for makes it much easier to decide what to drop when you are short of days.
bulletPoints: Kochi — usually the start or the end. Fort Kochi's colonial streets, the Chinese fishing nets, and an easy coastal pace to arrive into or leave from.
Munnar — the best-known hill station. Tea gardens, cool weather, viewpoints and waterfalls; comfortably two days.
Thekkady — Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary and the spice plantations. The nature-focused break in the middle of the trip.
Alleppey — the backwaters, and the houseboat night that is the single most requested thing in any Kerala package.
contentSections.highlightQuote: With more days you can add Kumarakom, Wayanad, Kovalam, Varkala, Vagamon or Bekal.

contentSections.heading: A five-day Kerala route, day by day
contentSections.content: Day 1: arrive in Kochi and drive up to Munnar, watching the landscape change as you climb; evening free. Day 2: a full day in Munnar — tea gardens, viewpoints, waterfalls, with time to stop for photographs. Day 3: Munnar to Thekkady through more hill country, with a spice plantation visit or an evening activity depending on arrival time. Day 4: Thekkady to Alleppey, check into the houseboat or a backwater-facing hotel, and cruise the canals into the evening. Day 5: back to Kochi for your flight or train. That is a shape, not a fixed booking — it stretches, shortens and rearranges, and Safar Trails' own Kerala trips are linked below.

contentSections.heading: Best time to visit Kerala
contentSections.content: There is no single best month; it depends on whether you are optimising for weather, price or quiet.
bulletPoints: October to February — the most comfortable window for sightseeing, cooler and drier in both the hills and the backwaters. It is also the busiest, so hotels and houseboats fill early.
March to May — warmer, especially in the lowlands and on the water, but fewer crowds. Munnar stays pleasant through it.
June to September — the monsoon. Everything is greener, it is the season people come for Ayurveda, and rates are lowest. Heavy rain can move a schedule, so keep the plan loose.

contentSections.heading: How to reach Kerala
contentSections.content: By air: Kerala has four airports — Cochin, Trivandrum, Calicut and Kannur. Which one suits you depends on the route; Cochin is usually right if the trip starts with Kochi and Munnar. By train: Ernakulam (Kochi), Thiruvananthapuram, Kozhikode and Kottayam are the main stations, well connected to most Indian cities. By road: Kerala is easy to reach from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka if you are driving in.

contentSections.heading: What a Kerala package costs, and why there is no single number
contentSections.content: Price moves with travel dates, number of travellers, nights, hotel category, vehicle type, which destinations are in, the meal plan, whether a houseboat is included, and any activities added. Packages usually tier into three: Budget, with 3-star stays, a standard vehicle and the essential sightseeing; Premium, with 4-star hotels and slightly better transport; and Luxury, with 5-star resorts, higher-end houseboats and a more curated trip. A generic figure would be wrong for most people, which is why it is quoted against your actual dates, group and hotel preference instead.

contentSections.heading: Included, and not included
contentSections.content: Worth reading before you pay rather than after. A Kerala package typically covers accommodation for the nights booked, breakfast as per the meal plan, private transport for sightseeing and the intercity drives, airport or station transfers, the sightseeing in the finalised itinerary, and the driver, parking and toll charges.
bulletPoints: Not included: flights and train tickets
Lunch and dinner, unless the meal plan says otherwise
Monument and attraction entry tickets
Adventure and optional activities
Camera or video charges at sightseeing spots
Travel insurance, personal expenses, and any sightseeing beyond the agreed itinerary
GST and applicable taxes, where not stated as included
contentSections.highlightQuote: You get the exact inclusions and exclusions in writing before you confirm. If a quote will not give you that list, that is the answer.

contentSections.heading: Hotels, vehicles and what fits your group
contentSections.content: Accommodation runs Standard (3-star and comfortable value stays), Premium (4-star hotels and resorts with more amenities) and Luxury (5-star resorts and premium houseboats). Actual hotels depend on availability, dates, location and budget. Transport is chosen by group size — a sedan for couples and small groups, an SUV for families, a tempo traveller for a larger group travelling together — and covers airport and station transfers plus the drives between Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and Alleppey.

contentSections.heading: Who Kerala suits, and how the plan changes
contentSections.content: Couples: hill-station stays, a houseboat night and a private vehicle make it an easy, unhurried trip. Honeymooners: Munnar's tea-garden resorts and the Alleppey houseboats, at a slower pace. Families: comfortable hotels, short drives and a flexible sightseeing rhythm, adjustable for young children or elderly parents. Friends and groups: a bigger vehicle and the freedom to add or drop stops. Senior travellers: fewer hours in the car, more time in each place.

contentSections.heading: Practical tips
contentSections.content: Small things that make a Kerala trip go smoothly.
bulletPoints: Book hotels and houseboats early in peak season — they genuinely run out.
Keep the plan flexible through the monsoon.
Pack light, breathable clothing, and rain protection from June to September.
Do not over-pack the itinerary. Kerala is better slow.
Confirm houseboat timings, meals and cabin type before you travel.
Carry original ID, comfortable footwear and some cash for small purchases.

contentSections.heading: Common questions
contentSections.content: How many days? Five to seven covers Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady and Alleppey comfortably; a seven-day version leaves room for Kumarakom, Wayanad or a coastal stop like Varkala. Two days is really only enough for one region — Kochi with a short backwater run, or Munnar on its own. For couples, Munnar plus Alleppey is the combination that works, with a beach stop added if you want one. Flights are not included by default, but they can be added to the quote if you would rather book everything together — send your departure city and dates. Travelling by train works just as well: the itinerary is planned around your arrival and departure stations, with transfers included.
